_README: GC winner's total race time per year, in seconds. Read by export_gc.py,
export_race_summary.py and export_all_races_summary.py; a year absent here
falls back to summing the winner's per-stage times, which understates any
edition missing some of them.
PROVENANCE (traced 2026-08-22). Source is PCS throughout, but this file was
never a script's output -- it was assembled by three separate operations, and
that is why nothing in this repo writes it:
68d585d 2026-07-17  created with 88 years, derived from the existing
giro_races_summary_overrides.json, which traces back to
check_giro_gc_times.py scraping PCS GC pages ->
giro_gc_time_corrections.json ->
apply_giro_gc_corrections.py.
8e8e2f0 2026-08-15  1959 and 1977 corrected (they read 41:14:17 and
65:29:01 against local medians of ~106:50). Correct
values 101:50:26 and 107:27:16, both read off PCS's own
GC classifications rather than taken on trust.
4f82d99 2026-08-15  13 missing years filled from PCS (1928, 1930, 1931,
checked against the historical record and each time
speed-checked against our stored distance; all 13 land
DELIBERATELY MISSING: 1946. PCS gives Bartali 65:32:20, which is 46.5 km/h
over 3,050 km -- impossible for the first post-war Giro and consistent with a
partial sum. Left absent rather than written, because it is not clear whether
the time or the distance is at fault.
THIS FILE IS CURATED, NOT SCRAPED. check_gc_times.py can regenerate a
winner-times file from a live PCS sweep, but only with --write-winner-times,
which check_giro_gc_times.py deliberately does NOT pass. A sweep would set
every year from PCS as-is -- which would reintroduce 1946's impossible value
and discard any future judgement of the same kind. Extend this file by hand,
verifying each value the way 4f82d99 did.
